RECORD each finding's disposition at reconcile time..." The csr protocol has no "external-claim verification" decision point in its round loop (lines 45-49); reconcile is about applying findings, not adjudicating external claims. The proposal is INTRODUCING a new decision point, not naming an existing one. The "implicit general-purpose use" is also not in csr's protocol — §1 itself characterizes it as an ad-hoc pattern in the node-bin incident ("the adjudicator-with-a-fetch-leg did not exist; a general-purpose spawn or author-fetch were the only options"), not a documented csr step.

Proposal: "on exhaustion return `unverifiable` with what was tried — never hunt unbounded (the bounded-observable doctrine, ADR #52 family)." ADR #52 in pd/references/design-decisions.md (verified): "The hetero substrate runs BOUNDED + OBSERVABLE — explicit `--max-turns` (print mode has NO default turn limit; the old 'CC's turn limit' citation was a phantom), DEFAULT stream-json read incrementally (stderr heartbeat + resolved-model capture + `--max-stream-bytes` runaway breaker + stderr tail), budget demoted to coarse breaker (default 12.0), `--no-stream` json fallback — CC v2.1.238 re-probe recorded". ADR #52 is specifically scoped to the hetero SUBSTRATE (CC subprocess supervision: argv, stream-json, byte-cap, stderr heartbeat, subprocess version re-probe). Extending it to a SUBAGENT's per-claim search budget stretches the original ADR's scope; the "family" wording acknowledges the extension but does not justify the analogy between subprocess supervision and an in-context subagent's tool-call budget.

Proposal §4 Role: "given ONE atomic factual claim or technical question (+ optional version/scope context), search, fetch the adjudicating source(s), and return a verdict grounded ONLY in fetched text." Proposal §4 Boundaries: "adjudicates FACTS/citations only; never judges whether the doc's thesis/conclusion is right (outcome axis stays human — family philosophy)." §1 example: "verify ONE atomic claim or technical constraint against the live web (e.g. 「核验 NLB ENI conntrack 约束」)". "Technical question" (Role) is broader than "FACTS/citations only" (Boundaries); a technical question can be a behavior, comparison, or constraint semantics, not all of which are pure facts/citations. The Boundaries would reject any non-fact-shaped input the Role says it accepts.

Proposal §2: `solidforge:doc-reviewer` row → "offline; reviews, never adjudicates facts". doc-reviewer.agent.md line 14 (verified): "contradiction — two claims in the doc conflict, or a claim conflicts with a cited source." doc-reviewer.agent.md line 15 (verified): "authority-chain-break — a claim cites a source that does not actually say what the doc says it says." doc-reviewer DOES adjudicate claims against cited sources (the contradiction and authority-chain-break kinds); "never adjudicates facts" is false. The accurate framing is "offline against cited sources only (no external web fetch)", not "never adjudicates facts".

Proposal §4: "Source tiers (output metadata): official vendor docs > RFC/standard > first-party engineering blog > community; label the tier of each source used." Actual `agents/claim-verifier.agent.md` frontmatter description (line 3) reads in full: "Given ONE atomic claim AND the fetched source text that adjudicates it, returns a verdict (verified / refuted / narrowed / unverifiable) grounded in a fetched-source quote. Fresh, independent context; never edits or fixes. Spawn it per-claim as the verdict step (PSV-I3) of a psv run. The fetched source TEXT is the oracle — not model recall." The truncation removes load-bearing content the doc later relies on: the verdict enum the doc cites as "psv's enum VERBATIM" (§4 line 36), the "grounded in a fetched-source quote" grounding (the very invariant the proposal builds on), and the "fetched source TEXT is the oracle — not model recall" phrasing (paraphrased in §4 line 32). Same-family r6 caught §4 schema-grounding and psv-quote issues but did not flag this §2-table truncation.

Doc states: "Multi-fetch collapse: the grounding block cites the fetch whose text DETERMINES the verdict (tier preference breaks ties only among determining fetches); every other fetch is listed in `searched`." But question mode (also defined in §4) has NO top-level `verdict` ("NO top-level `verdict`; a `findings[]` array..."). The "determining fetch" selection rule presupposes a verdict that question mode does not produce, and the doc provides no analogous selection criterion (per-finding strongest-fetch? per-finding tier-preference? aggregate best-fetch?) for question-mode grounding blocks. This is a load-bearing gap because every question-mode output with >1 fetch must pick a grounding block.

The gate is silent on (a) whether `refuted` verdicts on volatile-class facts also require an anchor (the doc elsewhere says refuted/narrowed already require a quote, but the volatile-class constraint is not reiterated), and (b) whether a `narrowed` verdict on a volatile fact must itself carry date/version scoping (vs. just a fetch quote).
